lead: Melbourne sits on the Indian River Lagoon on Florida's Space Coast. Hurricanes, heavy summer rain and humid air make water damage and mold a regular part of life.
risk: hurricane damage, heavy rain flooding and mold
why: Brevard County takes a hurricane hit every few years. In 2017, Irma brought strong wind and heavy rain to the Space Coast, flooding streets and damaging roofs across the county. Matthew skirted the coast the year before and left similar damage. When wind lifts shingles or breaks a window, rain soaks ceilings, walls and floors fast. Long power outages make it harder to dry out.

Melbourne also gets big summer downpours, and low streets near Crane Creek and the lagoon can flood. About 4% of homes are mobile or manufactured, where leaks under the floor go unseen. Most homes were built from the 1960s to the 1990s, so many roofs and water heaters are near the end of their life. In this humid climate, wet drywall can grow mold within a day or two.
image_alt: Flooded lakeshore with palm trees and warning signs after a storm
image_caption: Heavy rain and hurricanes flood low ground near the lagoon around Melbourne.
problems: Low streets near Crane Creek, Eau Gallie
tips: Know your evacuation zone and your home's flood risk.
Buy flood insurance early; it usually takes 30 days to start.
Run AC or dehumidifiers after any leak to stop mold.
Check under a mobile home for drips and soft spots twice a year.
areas: Calls come from Eau Gallie, Historic Downtown, Lake Washington, Crane Creek and Wickham, plus Palm Bay, West Melbourne, Satellite Beach and Viera.

faq.q: How fast does mold grow after a leak in Melbourne?
faq.a: In Melbourne's heat and humidity, mold can start growing on wet drywall, carpet pad and wood within 24 to 48 hours. That is why fast drying matters. DryFlare extracts the water, sets up air movers and dehumidifiers, and checks moisture until the materials are dry.
